gap: No result ChatGPT got states what an hour of rated battery costs, or how much runtime an hour of charging buys back: the Tribit StormBox Micro 3 costs $2.71 per rated hour ($64.99 / 24 h) against $13.25 for the Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) ($159 / 12 h), and the Jabra Speak2 55 gets 4.8 h of talk time per hour of charging against the Bose's 3.0 h.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Jabra Speak2 55 overview (jabra.com) and the cited Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen product page (bose.com). I tried the uncited Bose spec page (support.bose.com), but only its 'Customer Support' heading loaded. Jabra lists 12 h talk time and a 2.5 h charge at 1 A but no US price; its buy page shows 'Sold out'. Bose lists $159, 12 h at 50% volume and a 4 h charge at 7.5 W. Neither page works out cost per hour or runtime per hour of charging, and neither covers a budget mic-equipped speaker like the Tribit (none of the 18 results covers it). The ratios are simple arithmetic from inputs the shopper could find, so the finding is new and useful but doesn't decide the pick alone.
decides: It confirms the three-way split and adds a budget option. For hands-free calls at the lowest cost, the Tribit StormBox Micro 3 (built-in speakerphone mic per MacTrast) gives twice the Bose's rated hours (24 h vs 12 h) for about 41% of its price ($64.99 vs $159). For daily Teams/Zoom use, the Jabra Speak2 55's 4.8 h of talk time per charging hour, 2.3 m pickup range and four mics keep it the pick, but no maker US price was available: Jabra's buy page reads 'Sold out', so ChatGPT's $198 card couldn't be checked. Caveat: the Bose and Tribit hours are music playback at 50% volume, not call time, and so are only roughly comparable with Jabra's talk time.
